title: Foreigners Report Thousands of Seoul Taxi Overcharges
paragraphs: A taxi ride to the airport in an unfamiliar city can already be stressful — especially if you're worried you might arrive late! But for one Japanese tourist in Seoul, it also came with a huge bill.
The tourist took a taxi from Myeongdong in central Seoul to Gimpo International Airport, and was charged 480,000 won, or about $360. That's around 16 times the usual fare of 30,000 won, or about $22.
In a hurry to catch their flight, the tourist paid, but later filed a complaint. An investigation found the driver never turned on the meter, and entered the fare by hand after arriving.
And this was not an isolated case.
According to Seoul city government data, foreigners filed 6,481 complaints about possible taxi overcharging between 2021 and August 2026.
However, only 204 of those cases — about 3% — led to official action. Most of those drivers received warnings, while 26 had their licenses suspended, and two had them canceled.
But more than two-thirds of complaints were closed without penalties.
Seoul officials said some cases were difficult to investigate, especially when tourists had already left the country and could not be easily contacted. Some complaints were also withdrawn.

But the city has now introduced stricter penalties. Since September, drivers caught overcharging face a 30-day license suspension for a first offense, and 60 days for a second. A third offense can mean losing their license.
Previously, a first offense brought only a warning.
The issue comes as South Korea is heading for a record year for tourism. The country welcomed 15 million foreign visitors between January and August, up 22% from the same period in 2025.

Over the same period, credit card spending by foreign visitors in the tourism sector also rose 49% from a year earlier, reaching 14 trillion won, or about $10.5 billion — the highest level since records began.
